Subject: Re: Alder RFP 187 — additional clarifications (KMS / patching / operator roles)

Ben / Mina / Jonas —

A few clarifying points from TechOps and the procurement team:

- KMS: we need confirmation that the customer-managed HSM can host both root and data encryption keys and that key rotation can be automated via our KMS. Do you support HSM-backed key import and rotation APIs?
- Egress: For air-gapped installs we cannot have any outbound connections except to a signed update mirror under our control. Please confirm your offline patch delivery (signed artifacts) and the verification steps.
- Operator roles: we want clear separation between operator accounts and Redwood remote support accounts — what controls exist for ephemeral operator access and audit logging?
- Evidence: procurement expects SBOM attestations (per-release) and a traceable patch signature chain.

Attached: Alder_security_requirements.xls

Carla
Procurement — Alder Biomed
[Attachment: Alder_security_requirements.xls]

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Carla Spencer <carla.spencer@alderbio.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T11:52:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Alder RFP 187 — technical responses and evidence checklist

Carla —

Thanks — answering inline and attaching a short checklist: 

On 2026-12-02 08:34, Carla Spencer wrote:
> - KMS: we need confirmation that the customer-managed HSM can host both root and data encryption keys and that key rotation can be automated via our KMS. Do you support HSM-backed key import and rotation APIs?

Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed HSMs (PKCS#11 and cloud-KMS HSM providers). Supported modes:
- Customer-managed root keys (for disk and config encryption) and workload keys (per-deployment data keys).
- Automated rotation: we provide a rotation adapter that calls your KMS rotation API (schedules and triggers) and can be run in-airgap mode via a signed operator bundle.

> - Egress: For air-gapped installs we cannot have any outbound connections except to a signed update mirror under our control. Please confirm your offline patch delivery (signed artifacts) and the verification steps.

Confirmed. Offline patching workflow:
- We publish signed artifact bundles (SHA512 + vendor signature).
- Customer mirrors the bundle into an internal artifact repository.
- Operator runs local verification (we provide verification tooling and public key).
- For emergency hotfixes we provide an encrypted USB image process and a signed manifest you can verify prior to applying.

> - Operator roles: we want clear separation between operator accounts and Redwood remote support accounts — what controls exist for ephemeral operator access and audit logging?

Operator boundary:
- Operator roles are RBAC-based; Redwood support accounts are separate and only allowed when explicitly authorized by the customer (time-bound grant via signed approval token).
- Audit logging: all operator actions are logged locally and shipped to your telemetry collector; logs are tamper-evident (append-only signed log chain).

> - Evidence: procurement expects SBOM attestations (per-release) and a traceable patch signature chain.

We produce SBOM (CycloneDX) per release and will provide a signed attestation artifact. Patch bundles include a signed manifest; chain-of-trust info is in the manifest metadata.

Attached: secure-kms-config-checklist.pdf (HSM adapter options, sample config snippets)

Next steps:
- Ben will share a concise acceptance test plan and proposed kickoff slots for the technical review (we suggest a 90-minute technical review + 60-minute operator workshop).
- We’ll prepare a DocuSign DPA and a Drive folder with the signed artifacts and SBOMs.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: secure-kms-config-checklist.pdf]
